title: A Reliable and Reproducible Critical-Sized Segmental Femoral Defect Model in Rats Stabilized with a Custom External Fixator
protocol: Use outbred Sprague-Dawley male rats weighing approximately 350 g.
Reconstitute rhBMP-2 with sterile water to a concentration of 1.5 mg/mL.
Trim the rhBMP-2 soaked collagen sponge using sterile scissors and ruler to fit a 5 mm x 3 mm x 3 mm defect.
Distribute the rhBMP-2 solution evenly over the collagen sponge using a syringe.
Cut aluminum sheet stock (type 6061, 0.088” thickness) into two pieces (1.4” x 6”) using a jigsaw or appropriate tool.
Mount one piece in the milling machine and cut four 'V' grooves (0.035” deep) lengthwise using a 1/8” 90°-point carbide drill mill.
Leave the other piece free of cuts.
Cut individual plates of 0.3” width from two pieces.
Measure and drill screw holes for 4-40 thread on the plate with ‘V’ grooves.
Tap the plate with ‘V’ grooves using a 4-40 thread.
Drill the plate without grooves for a #4 screw body drill.
Sand both pieces to round corners and reduce weight.
Screw pieces together with 4-40, 18-8 stainless steel button head cap screws (0.25”) so that grooves are flush against the plain plate.
Induce anesthesia by placing the rat in an induction chamber delivering 4 L O2/min with 4% isoflurane.
Remove the rat from the chamber after it loses righting reflex.
Attach a nose cone and place the rat at the maintenance dose of anesthesia through the nose (O2 delivery rate to 2-3 L/min and 0.8% isoflurane).
Place the rat on a heating pad or under a warming light to prevent hypothermia.
Confirm adequate depth of anesthesia by pinching the toe or testing the palpebral reflex.
Apply lubrication to eyes to prevent drying out of the cornea.
Deliver a subcutaneous injection of extended-release buprenorphine (1 mg/kg) on the trunk/dorsum of the rat, far from the surgical site.
Shave area around hindleg using the 13th rib, the foot, the dorsal midline, and the ventral midline as margins.
Scrub shaved area using sterile 2 x 2 gauze soaked with 10% povidone-iodine followed by 70% EtOH (4 times each, alternating).
Administer an intramuscular injection of cefazolin (20 mg/kg) into the operative quadriceps.
Administer enrofloxacin (0.25 mg/ml) in drinking water for 7 days postoperatively for continued antibiotic protection.
Place rats on medicated feed (e.g., Uniprim) for the duration of the study to prevent pin tract infections.
Apply double antibiotic ointment to the skin-pin interface once daily for 3 days postoperatively.
Extend shaved leg through fenestrated, clear sticky drape and cover surgical bench in sterile towels to create a sterile field.
Palpate the femur and use a #15 blade to create an anterolateral incision through the skin extending from the patella to the greater trochanter at the proximal femur.
Carefully incise the lateral leg fascia along the intermuscular septum.
Separate the vastus lateralis muscle from the hamstrings until the lateral femur is exposed.
Preserve the abductor gluteal tendon insertion on the greater trochanter.
Perform a careful, atraumatic circumferential soft tissue dissection to expose the femur at its mid-diaphysis.
Use a #15 blade to gently cut muscle away from the underlying bone while keeping the blade parallel against the bone surface.
Lift the dissected muscle with a periosteal elevator and proceed around the femoral shaft until 7-10 mm of central diaphysis is cleared of soft tissue on all sides.
Insert four 1.0 mm Kirschner wires: two proximal and two distal in the femur, perpendicular to the lateral femur directed straight from lateral to medial.
Ensure all pins engage both cortices for adequate stability.
Start with the distal-most pin first, just at the level of the lateral epicondyle.
Place jig flush to the lateral distal femur and insert a 1.0 threaded tip k-wire.
Maintain the position of the jig on the bone.
Identify where the most proximal pin will enter the bone based on the jig holes.
Carefully incise parallel to the fibers of the gluteal tendon as needed to create a small gap in the tissue for the proximal pin to pass through, thus minimizing iatrogenic damage to the tendon.
Drill a 1.0 mm non-threaded k-wire in this gap, ensuring the pin engages both cortices.
Maintain the jig’s position in contact with the bone.
Drill two 1.0 mm threaded k-wires, one on either side of the future defect site, ensuring pins engage both cortices.
Place the external fixator bar level 1 cm above skin and screw tightly, locking the bar in place.
Clip the excess pin lengths.
Prepare for the ostectomy (defect creation) by placing a small, curved retractor around the anterior and posterior femur to protect the surrounding soft tissue, muscle, and neurovascular bundle.
Utilizing a ~5 mm sagittal oscillating saw blade, very cautiously create a 5 mm segmental defect through the mid-diaphysis.
Apply light, even pressure with the saw to avoid unnecessary fracture.
Apply small amounts of irrigation using room temperature 0.9% sterile normal saline while creating the defect to avoid thermal necrosis of the bone.
Flush the wound with 10 mL of normal saline after creating the defect.
Administer 0.1 mL of a 0.25% bupivacaine with epinephrine (1:200,000) to the wound as an analgesic and vasoconstrictor.
Insert the scaffold (5 mm x 3 mm x 3 mm) into the defect.
Close the muscle plane using a simple interrupted pattern with 4-0 absorbable suture.
Close the skin layer using a running subcuticular pattern with 4-0 absorbable suture and skin glue to close gaps around the protruding pins.
Monitor the rat continuously until it can consistently maintain an upright posture after surgery.
Mix 10 µL of mRNA encoding for Gaussia luciferase (stock concentration of 1 µg/µL) with 30 µL of the lipidic transfecting agent.
Incubate mRNA-lipid complexes for at least 5 min at room temperature to form complexes.
Store complexes in ice if not used immediately, for a maximum of 1 h.
Pipette half the volume of mRNA complexes using a 20 µL pipette with filtered tips.
Inject half the volume of mRNA complexes to the distal end of the defect.
Inject the remaining half-volume of mRNA complexes to the proximal end of the defect.
The following day, anesthetize the rat using inhaled isoflurane as previously described.
Position the anesthetized rat in an imaging chamber with a nose cone delivering maintenance isoflurane (0.8% isoflurane).
Inject coelenterazine resuspended in saline at a dose of 4 mg/kg body weight near the defect.
Acquire bioluminescence images using the IVIS system according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Calibrate the plain radiographic machine and prepare the X-ray imaging system.
Anesthetize the rat using inhaled isoflurane as previously described.
Position the anesthetized rat in a nose cone with maintenance isoflurane (0.8% isoflurane).
Capture anteroposterior (AP) femur radiograph of the rat.
Place the rat in sternal recumbency.
Advance the surgical hindlimb forward, flexing at the hip and stifle joint.
Flex the stifle joint to approximately 90°.
Tape the paw plantar side down, close to the body wall.
Position the tibia forward from the femur to eliminate superimposing bones.
Place a translucent sponge in the groin region for slight abduction of the hip.
Obtain an anterior-posterior (cranial-caudal) image of the femur.
Repeat the AP femur radiographic view immediately following surgery, at 4 weeks, and at 12 weeks.
Use tape and gauze to position the animal’s extremity appropriately for quality and consistent imaging.
Remove the rat from the nose cone and monitor continuously until the rat can consistently maintain an upright posture.
Place the rat back into the cage after monitoring.
Euthanize rats in a chamber with inhaled CO2 according to AVMA ethical standards.
Shave the hindlimb, remove skin from the operative extremity.
Disarticulate femur at the hip following euthanasia.
Carefully remove all soft tissue from the operative femur (including muscles, tendons, and ligaments).
Leave only a thin layer of muscle surrounding the defect site to protect the healing region.
Place the femur in 10% Neutral Buffered Formalin at room temperature for 3-4 days with a 15:1 formalin to tissue volume ratio.
Change the solution once halfway through the fixation process.
Decalcify the femur in a 15% Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) pH 6.5 solution for 3-4 weeks.
Collect serial radiographs to determine decalcification endpoint.
Bisect the femur longitudinally with a cut from anterior to posterior in the mid-sagittal plane.
Submit tissue for standard paraffin embedding and hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining.
Send H&E slides to a pathologist for histological assessment.
